turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he could not bear the thought of living without her, that she was his wife and the mother of their son, and that he would do everything in his power to make her last days comfortable and peaceful.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the maid to fetch her the embroidered box from the top shelf, where her own wedding dress was kept.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan that she didn't need to worry about anything, that he would take care of her and the household, and that Father would be there to support them too.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung and the eldest son, her eyes clouding with worry, and told them that she had not yet seen the girl they had chosen for the eldest son's marriage, and that she wanted to meet her and make sure she was worthy of their family.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son reassured O-lan that he would not think of marrying until she had given her approval and seen the girl for herself, and that he was willing to wait as long as it took for her to be satisfied.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she would go and fetch the embroidered box immediately, and that she would make sure to polish the silver hinges so that they would shine like new.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung to show her the girl's family's farm, so that she could see for herself if they were worthy of their family's bloodline.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would take her to see the girl's family's farm as soon as possible, but that she should not worry about these things now, for her health was more important than anything else.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung, you must promise me that the girl's family's farm is prosperous and worthy of our family's name, I must see it for myself before I give my blessing.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid asked O-lan if there was anything else she could do for her before she left to rest.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan must not worry about the girl's family's farm, for he would take care of everything and make sure that their son is married off to a worthy bride.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would be content only when she had seen the girl's family's farm with her own eyes and given her blessing.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he was confident that the girl's family's farm was indeed prosperous, and that he would go with his father to the farm as soon as possible, so that she could see it for herself.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung, you must not try to comfort me now, I must see the girl's family's farm for myself, it is the only thing that will bring me peace

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung firmly told O-lan that she would not be leaving this house until he had made her a promise that he would bring their son to the girl's family's farm, so that she could see it for herself.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would not rest until the girl's family's farm was inspected, and that he must take their son to see it, no matter how far or difficult the journey may be

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son asked his mother, 'But Mother, are you not tiring yourself too much with all these arrangements? Should we not wait until you are stronger before we make this journey?'

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that they must leave at once, for she had a feeling that she would not be able to travel when the spring rains came

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung firmly instructed O-lan that she would not be leaving the house, that she would exhaust herself needlessly if she insisted on going to the girl's family's farm

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his father that he understood his mother's wishes and that he was willing to go to the girl's family's farm with him, as long as they could persuade his mother to stay behind and rest.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
